name: Tesler's Law
axiom: Every system carries irreducible complexity; design moves it between the system and the user.
trigger: People are asked to supply details the product could derive, such as time zones, currency formats, or bank codes.
checklist: Derive time zones, currency formats, and country codes from context instead of prompting.
Resolve file type, encoding, and MIME parameters during upload rather than asking.
Ship production-ready defaults for advanced settings so people opt out, not in.

antiPattern.violation: An international payment form asks customers for SWIFT, routing, clearing, and branch details by hand.
antiPattern.remediation: Accept the IBAN and resolve the bank name, branch, and routing codes in the backend.

parametricParams.caption: COMPLEXITY MOVES; THE TOTAL DOES NOT
